source_row.stem: A client is diagnosed with Hashimoto's thyroiditis, an autoimmune condition, and a family member assumes autoimmune destruction of the thyroid would logically cause the gland to produce too much hormone rather than too little. The nurse should anticipate this condition typically instead leads to:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Hyperthyroidism exclusively, since autoimmune thyroid destruction is thought by the family member to typically raise hormone output","B":"Immediate, complete thyroid failure within days, rather than the gradual decline over a longer period that actually characterizes this condition","C":"No meaningful effect on thyroid function, despite the known autoimmune destruction of thyroid tissue occurring in this condition","D":"Hypothyroidism over time, as autoimmune destruction progressively impairs thyroid hormone production"}}
source_row.rationale: Hashimoto's thyroiditis is an autoimmune condition that typically leads to hypothyroidism over time, as progressive autoimmune destruction of thyroid tissue impairs hormone production.
